meta_title: Frequently asked questions | Margarita Makri, Psychologist
meta_description: Answers about psychotherapy, CBT, duration, confidentiality and the practical side of sessions.
title: Frequently asked questions
lead: This information is general and does not replace an individual assessment.

items.q: How do I know I need psychotherapy?
items.a: You do not need a “serious problem” to see a psychologist. If something has troubled you for a while, affects your mood, sleep, relationships or work, or you simply want to understand yourself better, a first meeting can help.

items.q: How is psychotherapy different from talking to a friend?
items.a: Psychotherapy is a professional, confidential and structured process with a clear framework and goals. The therapist is trained to understand difficulties and suggest evidence-based ways of dealing with them, without judging you.
Psychologists do not prescribe medication. The need for medication is assessed by a psychiatrist, and when needed we work together, always with your consent.

items.q: What if I do not feel I am a good fit with the therapist?
items.a: A good therapeutic relationship matters. You can talk about it openly, and if needed, I will recommend another professional.

It is a structured psychotherapy that focuses on the links between thoughts, feelings and behaviour, and gives practical tools for difficulties such as anxiety and depression. [More about the approach](/en/approach/).

items.q: Which difficulties can it help with?
items.a: Research support is particularly strong for anxiety disorders and good for depression. It is also used for stress, sleep and other issues. Whether it suits you is assessed individually.
There is no timeframe that fits everyone. Some people notice small changes in the first weeks, especially when they practise between sessions. Others need longer. We track progress together.
It depends on the difficulty and your goals. According to the UK's NHS, a course of CBT usually lasts between 5 and 20 sessions, but the number is tailored to each person and decided together.
Usually yes, in the form of small exercises or observations between sessions. That is where new skills are put into practice, and they are always adapted to your time.

items.q: What is the first session like?
items.a: It is an introduction. We talk about what brings you, your history and what you would like to change. I explain how we work and answer questions, so you can decide whether to continue. No preparation is needed.

items.q: How long is a session, and how often?

items.a: Yes, they are covered by professional confidentiality. The limited exceptions are set by law and professional ethics, such as a serious and immediate risk to life. For adolescents there are specific arrangements for informing parents, which we discuss from the start.
For many people they are a practical and suitable option. You need a quiet, private space and a stable connection. If they do not suit your situation, we will talk about it.
